transcript.text: I can certainly help you troubleshoot your hob. 'Not working properly' could mean a few different things, but the most common causes are usually simple settings or a specific zone failing. First, please check if there is a child lock symbol (often a key or padlock icon) lit up on the display. Many hobs have this feature which disables all controls for safety; holding that button for a few seconds often unlocks it. Also, could you confirm what type of hob you have? Is it an induction hob with a smooth glass top and digital touch controls, or is it ceramic radiant (glow red) or solid plate (coil)? This distinction helps me guide the next steps safely.
It's a ceramic one, the kind that glows red. No padlock symbol showing, and three of the rings work fine. Just the rear right one isn't heating up.

The most likely cause is either that specific heating element has burnt out or its control switch (energy regulator) has failed. To distinguish between these, we need to look inside. Please unplug the hob from the wall and wait for it to cool completely. If you are handy with tools, you can remove the glass top to inspect the rear right radiant element directly. Look for a broken coil or a dark burnt mark on that specific ring. If you cannot access the internals safely, please provide the brand and model number (usually found on a sticker under the hob or in your manual) so I can advise on the next steps.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Zanussi, and the manual says the model starts ZHRN but I don't have the rest. I'm not taking the glass top off though, I'd rather not mess with it.

The most likely cause is that the radiant heating element (the bulb itself) has burnt out, though there is a smaller chance the control switch for that zone has failed. As you’d prefer not to remove the glass top, I can’t inspect the internals directly. However, if the element were cracked or visibly broken on the surface, you would likely see it without taking anything apart. If the glass looks intact and clean around that ring, the internal component is faulty. To fix this properly, a qualified engineer will need to remove the hob top to replace either the heating bulb or its regulator switch. Please note that while you wait for an engineer, do not use that rear right zone if you suspect any damage to the glass surface, as moisture could reach live parts. You can safely continue using the other three rings.
